studies.title: ABFR-KAN: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Functional Brain Analysis
studies.modality: four-dimensional resting-state fMRI
studies.taxonomy_basis: KAN variants replace MLP components in the ViT patch encoder, the classification head, or both after in-pipeline fMRI patch sampling and functional-connectivity construction
studies.kan_role: ABFR-KAN samples multi-scale gray-matter patch time series directly from rs-fMRI, constructs anchor-based connectivity features, and classifies ASD using a ViT whose MLP and/or head is replaced by one of five KAN variants.
studies.datasets: ABIDE I DPARSF data from NYU (171 participants: 73 ASD, 98 controls) and University of Michigan (110: 55/55). Five-fold single-site evaluation and bidirectional held-site testing were reported.
studies.comparison: Compared with SVM, graph/CNN/transformer baselines and a RandomFR precursor. Focused experiments compare the MLP baseline with Efficient-, Fast-, Faster-, wavelet-, and Chebyshev-KAN in encoder/head configurations, and separately vary backbone, anchor selection, and iterative sampling.
studies.results: Best single-site ACC/AUC was 0.7427/0.7041 at NYU (FastKAN) and 0.7727/0.7184 at UM (Wav-KAN), versus MLP 0.7079/0.6544 and 0.7182/0.6426. Cross-site ACC/AUC was 0.5517/0.7181 for NYU-to-UM and 0.5707/0.5714 for UM-to-NYU; in the former direction, RandomFR accuracy was higher at 0.6109.
studies.evidence_basis: Multiple KAN variants and encoder/head placements are directly compared with an MLP configuration under the same fMRI representation pipeline, including cross-site testing, although per-site model selection and capacity/training-time matching remain incomplete.
studies.limitations: Small two-site preprint study; the best KAN family/configuration is selected separately for each site after many comparisons, increasing optimism. One-tailed tests over five cross-validation folds do not address fold dependence or multiple testing. Cross-site performance is mixed, KAN variants are not consistently superior, training time/parameters increase, and learned KAN functions are not analyzed for neurobiological meaning despite interpretability claims.
studies.direction_basis: The report contains discordant result directions across datasets, endpoints, or comparator configurations, or a performance gain accompanied by a resource or secondary-endpoint cost.

studies.title: Fully Kolmogorov-Arnold Deep Model in Medical Image Segmentation
studies.modality: breast ultrasound, colorectal-gland histopathology, and colonoscopy
studies.taxonomy_basis: Shared-activation KAN convolutional layers and grad-free splines replace conventional layers throughout the deep U-shaped encoder--decoder
studies.kan_role: ALL U-KAN combines Shared-activation KAN, grad-free spline computation, and deep KAN convolution to construct an almost fully KA-based segmentation network.
studies.datasets: BUSI 647 tumor images, GlaS 165 images, and CVC-ClinicDB 612 frames. Each was randomly split 80/20 for training/validation and evaluated over three fixed seeds; patient, source-section, and colonoscopy-sequence grouping were not reported.
studies.comparison: Compared with seven U-shaped models. BUSI ablations directly compare U-KAN with all KAN layers replaced by MLP, ordinary U-KAN, shared-activation/grad-free variants, and deep ALL U-KAN, including parameters, memory, and time.
studies.results: Across three seeds, ALL U-KAN reported IoU/F1 66.14+/-5.43/78.64+/-5.33 on BUSI, 88.72+/-0.23/94.00+/-0.07 on GlaS, and 85.37+/-0.06/91.98+/-0.02 on CVC. In one BUSI split it reached 69.43/81.82 with 3.17M parameters.
studies.evidence_basis: MLP-replacement, partial-KAN, and deep-KAN variants provide a focused component comparison, but SaKAN, grad detachment, depth, parameterization, and effective compute all change and the strongest result is a compound design.
studies.limitations: Random image/frame splits risk patient/slide/video leakage; no independent test or significance analysis. The dataset paragraph incorrectly describes GlaS using CVC-like 612-frame/31-sequence details, and ALL U-KAN training remains about fivefold slower per step than the MLP variant despite memory savings.

studies.title: KACNet: Enhancing CNN feature representation with Kolmogorov-Arnold networks for medical image segmentation and classification
studies.modality: ultrasound, histopathology, endoscopy, CT, MRA, and electron microscopy
studies.taxonomy_basis: KANConv repeatedly augments the main CNN encoder and is followed by ConvNeXt/token-KAN processing for both 2D segmentation and 3D classification
studies.kan_role: KACNet combines convolutional sampling, B-spline KAN feature interaction, ConvNeXt/residual processing, and token-KAN layers in a shared encoder for 2D segmentation and 3D classification.
studies.datasets: Five 2D segmentation datasets: BUSI 647 (452/129/66), GlaS 165 (115/33/17), CVC-ClinicDB 612 (428/122/62), DDTI 637 (445/65/127), and TN3K 3,493 (2,303/576/614). Six MedMNIST3D classification subsets were also used; the Synapse table reports 1,759 samples although its listed split sums to 759.
studies.comparison: Compared with multiple U-Net/CNN/KAN baselines for segmentation and ResNet/AutoML baselines for 3D classification. Projection ablations compared KANConv with Conv, CBAM, and ELA, and additional experiments deleted one or all KANConv layers.
studies.results: KACNet reported Dice/mIoU 82.99/70.93 on DDTI and 88.72/79.71 on TN3K; IoU/F1 were 65.05/78.55 on BUSI, 88.23/93.73 on GlaS, and 85.37/92.00 on CVC. Removing one KANConv layer reduced BUSI IoU from 0.6557 to 0.6334 and CVC IoU from 0.8549 to 0.8255.
studies.evidence_basis: KAN-focused projection and layer-deletion ablations were reported across three datasets, but KANConv remains a compound convolution--KAN operator and complete deletion materially changes model capacity.
studies.limitations: No external or prospective validation and patient-level grouping is not documented for the 2D splits. The SynapseMNIST3D sample total is internally inconsistent, performance is not uniformly best across the six 3D tasks, and the hybrid KAN/ConvNeXt/residual design limits pure KAN attribution.
studies.direction_basis: The report describes the KAN-containing full model as better than the named principal comparator(s) on its focal endpoint(s). This direction does not isolate the incremental effect of KAN.

studies.title: Trustworthy Longitudinal Brain MRI Completion: A Deformation-Based Approach with KAN-Enhanced Diffusion Model
studies.modality: longitudinal T1-weighted brain MRI
studies.taxonomy_basis: KAN blocks recur within the diffusion network that predicts deformation fields for longitudinal MRI completion
studies.kan_role: DF-DiffCom uses a KAN-enhanced diffusion backbone to predict age-conditioned deformation fields and a flexible temporal-information encoder to incorporate a variable number of prior scans.
studies.datasets: OASIS-3: 2,535 T1 MRI scans from 634 subjects, split by subject 70% training/20% test/10% validation. TransMorph pseudo-target and brain-age critic models used a separate non-overlapping subject subset.
studies.comparison: Compared with cGAN, DiffuseMorph, LoCI-DiffCom, and TADM. A 2x2 ablation adds DiffKAN and flexible guidance separately and jointly, directly exposing the small standalone KAN increment and larger interaction.
studies.results: Full DF-DiffCom reported PSNR 25.52+/-1.21 and SSIM 0.845+/-0.03 versus TADM 20.51+/-1.43/0.72+/-0.05. In ablation, baseline 23.73/0.794 changed to 24.01/0.796 with DiffKAN alone, 24.07/0.798 with guidance alone, and 25.52/0.845 jointly.
studies.evidence_basis: A factorial ablation isolates a small standalone DiffKAN change and a larger DiffKAN--guidance interaction, but the headline gain is compound and depends on pseudo-deformation supervision, diffusion, and a brain-age critic.
studies.limitations: Subject-level partitioning is strong, but deformation targets come from pretrained TransMorph rather than observed future anatomy. No independent cohort, diagnostic-reader study, downstream quantitative benefit, or calibration is reported; qualitative ventricular shrinkage is acknowledged as possibly a slice-selection artifact.

studies.title: CEST MRI data analysis using Kolmogorov‐Arnold network (KAN) and Lorentzian‐KAN (LKAN) models
studies.modality: CEST MRI (voxel-wise Z-spectra)
studies.taxonomy_basis: KAN/LKAN directly parameterizes the signal-to-quantitative-parameter mapping for CEST Z-spectra
studies.kan_role: A B-spline KAN and a Lorentzian-basis LKAN map each 43-point voxel Z-spectrum to nine MPLF-derived CEST fitting parameters.
studies.datasets: Single-slice 3T brain CEST MRI from 27 healthy volunteers; 25 participants supplied 548,865 spectra for training/validation (80/20), and two participants supplied 51,977 held-out test spectra.
studies.comparison: MLP, KAN, and LKAN were compared in approximately parameter-matched one-layer size groups and 2--5-layer variants; MPLF was the fitting reference. Models were trained five times, with added noise-robustness experiments.
studies.results: Versus MLP, KAN and LKAN reduced average test loss by 28.37% and 32.17%; LKAN reduced average test loss by 5.29% and training time by 37.26% versus KAN. Network inference for one slice was about 0.9 s versus about 5 min for MPLF.
studies.evidence_basis: Direct MLP--KAN and KAN--LKAN replacements were examined across approximate parameter groups, but the reference targets were MPLF-derived rather than independent ground truth.
studies.limitations: Single-center, single-scanner study of 27 healthy volunteers with only two held-out participants; MPLF supplies pseudo-reference targets rather than biological ground truth; no diseased cohort or external validation; KAN/LKAN training was slower than MLP.

studies.datasets: BraTS 2024 GLI contains 1,350 labelled post-treatment glioma cases, randomly divided into 1,080 training, 135 validation, and 135 test cases; four MRI modalities were used per subject.
studies.comparison: Compared with U-Net, Attention U-Net, SwinUNETR, and U-KAN. Extensive ablations change PFA, attention type/placement, and dynamic versus fixed loss weights, but never replace or remove the underlying U-KAN KAN stages.
studies.results: UKAN-EP test Dice for NETC/SNFH/ET/RC/WT was 0.5197/0.8887/0.6149/0.6924/0.9001 versus U-KAN 0.4526/0.8810/0.6152/0.6860/0.8927; uncertainties were reported as 1.96 standard errors.
studies.evidence_basis: The experiment identifies PFA, attention, and loss-weighting effects on top of U-KAN, not KAN versus a matched non-KAN model; therefore it supports the compound extension but not an independent KAN advantage.
studies.limitations: Single benchmark with random internal split and no center/scanner-held-out or prospective validation. Gains are small or mixed across subregions, and several attention/loss choices were explored on the same development data; the method uses slightly more GFLOPs/parameters than U-KAN.
